newsitem.title: USA: Raines sees continued U.S. growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Raines sees continued U.S. growth, low inflation.

text.p: U.S. Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines said on Tuesday that he sees continued growth in the U.S. economy with low inflation.
Speaking to a small group of reporters, Raines repeated that he expects the U.S. fiscal 1997 budget deficit projection to be revised downwards, saying: "It'll be noticeable."

Referring to forecasts in the president's budget, which is scheduled to be released in February, Raines said: "There will be some moving around of numbers but there's no dramatic change in our outlook on the economy. We look for continuing growth with low inflation for as far as the eye can see."
Raines said that there is always some risk of a recession, but that the administration did not see any of the telltale signs that one was in the offing.
"There is always a risk of a recession over any four-year period and particularly when you've had such a long expansion -- so that risk is always there," he said.

"The mitigating factor is that the kinds of things that typically lead to recessions don't appear to be occuring now and so we may be able to avoid recession for longer than most people have thought," he added.

"We don't see inventories getting out of line, we don't see speculative borrowing, and we have not had external shocks -- and so the kinds of things that have led to recession in the past don't appear to be on the horizon," he said.
"It doesn't mean they can't come on the horizon fairly rapidly, but so far this has been a very balanced expansion and, as long as it stays balanced, it can continue," he added.

Asked if there would be any significant revision to the administration's inflation forecasts, Raines replied: "Nothing dramatic. I think our estimates going forward are going to look very mainstream and I would assume that (those of the Congressional Budget Office) will look equally mainstream."
The last projection on the fiscal 1997 U.S. budget deficit based on current services was made in March, when the figure was put at $144 billion, an OMB official said.

In its midsession budget review, released in July, OMB estimated the fiscal year 1997 deficit at $125.7 billion, but the official said that was based on President Bill Clinton's balanced budget plan rather than on current services.
